decisions.story_title: SSCMS 7.2.0 through 7.4.0 arbitrary file read via layerImageUpload (CVE-2026-129539)
decisions.reason: CVE record published 16 Nov 2026 (assigner VulnCheck) describes an external control of file name or path in siteserver SSCMS 7.2.0 through 7.4.0 reached through the layerImageUpload endpoint: any authenticated registered user can read arbitrary server files. CVSS 4.0 7.1 (v3.1 6.5), network, low privileges, high confidentiality impact. Substance is in the CVE record itself; reported as not known to be exploited.

Polish-language Sekurak report on APT targeting of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN using CVE-2026-20127 to take over devices. Same CVE, implant and campaign already tracked in the canonical KeyDrift story. Duplicate of the second sekurak Mastodon post in this window; English translation will cover it.
Second copy of the same Sekurak Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN / CVE-2026-20127 article posted minutes earlier. Amalgamates into the existing KeyDrift story, no new substance.

The Hacker News account of the Cursor postmortem on the malicious Claude Code VS Code extension: a stolen Fireworks AI access key led to trojanized extension builds served to users. Identical incident to the canonical extension-backdoor story.
BleepingComputer follow-up: Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants affecting three wallet models and ships a fix. Directly advances the existing Trezor implant story.
Dark Reading piece on ArcticRAT using AI to profile victim finances, the story this candidate already covers.

Polish Sekurak report on KeePassXC 2.8.0 fixing security bugs including CVE-2026-69150, a heap use-after-free in the legacy KeePass 1 (.kdb) importer. Same release and CVE as the existing KeePassXC story; CVE record confirms the affected range below 2.8.0-beta1.
Duplicate Sekurak post of the KeePassXC 2.8.0 article. Same story.

decisions.story_title: Coles and Woolworths disclose cyber incidents within hours of each other
decisions.reason: news.com.au reporting that Australian grocery rivals Coles and Woolworths each disclosed a cybersecurity incident hours apart, with Coles saying customer data remains safe while it investigates. Two named companies, a live investigation, and an open question about a shared managed service provider. Social amplification of a named-outlet report; not commentary.
Weekly CVE tally roundup (4,647 new CVEs, 12 added to CISA KEV for Nov 9-15). Aggregated statistics, no single event to cover; KEV additions already tracked per-CVE.

NoisyTCP / CVE-2026-99288 detail post from the same outlet already in the existing story: pre-auth remote kernel panic, fixed in 6.12.117, 6.18.63 and 7.3.4. Corroborated independently by fosslinux.com, iTnews and vuldb, so it strengthens rather than duplicates.

decisions.story_title: Apache Shiro authentication bypass CVE-2026-129349 lets any password work after one login
decisions.reason: CVE-2026-129349, published 14 Nov 2026 by Apache (oss-security disclosure by Lenny Primak): DefaultLdapRealm accepts any password for a cached user once authentication caching is enabled, CVSS 9.1, fixed in Shiro 3.0.1 and 3.0.2. A public PoC has circulated on GitHub. No existing candidate story covers Shiro or the APISIX fixes mentioned.

SecurityWeek coverage of the law enforcement takedown of Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC infrastructure. Same operation as the canonical story; adds credential-checking and MFA advice but no new technical detail.

decisions.story_title: TrustFall CVE-2026-88235: public PoC abuses Windows TrustedInstaller to act as SYSTEM
decisions.reason: CVE-2026-88235 is a Microsoft elevation-of-privilege flaw (CVSS 7.8, published 10 Nov 2026, fixed in the November 2026 servicing stack updates) with a public proof of concept at github.com/crisprss/CVE-2026-88235 that abuses TrustedInstaller for SYSTEM-level write. Verified against the CVE record and the researcher PoC repository. No existing story covers it.
Self-promotional post advertising a training academy with no security event, vulnerability or advisory content.
Open-source project release announcement (forensic evidence sealer). Tooling marketing, no incident or vulnerability to cover.

decisions.story_title: Suspected cyber incident disrupts e-filing at California superior courts in Alameda and Kern counties
decisions.reason: DysruptionHub reporting (15 Nov 2026) that Alameda and Kern county superior courts lost electronic filing and online case search after notices of a possible cyber incident, with Kern's online payment system also down and Alameda working with case-management vendor Journal Technologies. Named courts, named vendor, live outage with service impacts. Same outage also hit Los Angeles filings through Journal Technologies.
SANS ISC Stormcast episode page for 16 Nov 2026, already ingested as this candidate story; the RSS copy only adds the direct audio link.
